claims.text: NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 has a predominantly single-phase BCC structure in the proposed initial state.
The untreated baseline has received no post-casting precipitation treatment.
The proposed intervention consists of solution treatment near 1100 °C, rapid quenching, and aging near 700 °C for 2–4 hours under inert atmosphere.
Solution treatment and rapid quenching will create a homogeneous solid solution in NbTaHfTiZrV0.5.
Aging at approximately 700 °C for 2–4 hours will induce controlled nanoscale carbide or intermetallic precipitation.
The treatment will produce uniformly distributed TiC or Zr-rich intermetallic precipitates within the BCC matrix.
The precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
The precipitate dispersion will refine or strengthen grain boundaries.
Precipitate obstruction of dislocation motion will increase alloy strength and mechanical durability.
The nanoscale precipitates will obstruct creep deformation and reduce the room-temperature creep strain rate.
Precipitates at grain boundaries and near surfaces will alter oxide-scale composition and promote TiO2 or ZrO2 formation.
The altered protective oxide layer will improve resistance to pitting and corrosion.
The two-step-treated alloy will have greater yield strength than the untreated baseline.
The two-step-treated alloy will have a lower room-temperature creep strain rate than the untreated baseline.
The two-step-treated alloy will have a higher pitting potential than the untreated baseline.
Careful control of aging time and temperature is necessary to avoid precipitate coarsening or embrittlement.
The proposed improvements should persist from ambient to moderately elevated aerospace operating temperatures in corrosive environments.
The strength benefit may be offset by embrittlement, and corrosion performance may vary with precipitate chemistry, distribution, and test environment.

contradictions.description: The experimental design specifies only a standard single-step group and a two-step group, but the falsification rule requires comparison with both the single-step group and an untreated baseline. No untreated group is included in the stated design.
